title: Nscale signs $3.5 billion, up-to-100,000-GPU compute deal with humanoid-robot maker Figure
subtitle: The multi-year partnership on NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform will train Figure's Helix models — with an initial Barstow, Texas deployment in H2 2027 and a path to scale beyond $6 billion.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Humanoid-robot maker Figure signed a strategic partnership with UK-based GPU cloud provider Nscale on September 3, committing to an initial $3.5 billion of AI compute with a plan to scale the deal past $6 billion. The infrastructure — up to 100,000 next-generation NVIDIA GPUs on the Vera Rubin platform — will train Figure's Helix models, the vision-language-action models that drive its humanoid robots. Initial deployment is scheduled for the second half of 2027 in Barstow, California, and Nscale is taking an equity stake in Figure as part of the deal.

The size is the story. Figure has raised roughly $1.9 billion in total equity to date, and has now committed almost twice that in compute — a structure only possible because Nscale is trading balance-sheet risk for both equity upside and preferred-supplier status. It is also one of the first compute-for-equity swaps between a GPU cloud and a robotics foundation-model company, following the pattern set by OpenAI-Microsoft and Anthropic-Amazon but adapted for physical AI. The 100,000-GPU figure puts the deployment on the same order of magnitude as the largest LLM training clusters running today.

The strategic bet Nscale is making is that Helix and its successors will be to humanoid robots what GPT-class models became to text — a general-purpose backbone that gets fine-tuned per task, per household, per factory. That would require far more compute per model generation than a single-purpose robot policy, and it would put Figure alongside Tesla Optimus, Unitree, and Apptronik as one of the handful of teams that can plausibly build such a model. The Vera Rubin platform choice matters too — Figure is not betting on today's Blackwell hardware but on NVIDIA's 2027-generation compute, which extends the training-and-deployment timeline by roughly two years.

For learners: a compute-for-equity deal is a very specific bet. Nscale gets guaranteed utilization on capacity it must build anyway, a stake in a company it thinks will be worth far more than its current $39B private valuation, and a marquee customer that lets it raise cheaper capital for the next data-center buildout. Figure gets compute it could not otherwise finance without diluting equity holders further. Watch how many more of these deals get signed in the next six months — if the pattern spreads, it means AI infrastructure is being financed less like a software business and more like a utility.
